code_binding.relationship: TRANSCRIBED VERBATIM. pd12.py is a top-level script with no callable core; importing it would execute a full production run against hard-coded scratchpad paths, so exact reuse is technically impossible. The transcription is PROVEN by exact replay, not asserted.

HISTORICAL_REPLAY.method: PARTITIONED BY k (exactly equivalent to monolithic)
HISTORICAL_REPLAY.why_partitioned: the monolithic form spilled 23 GB of temp and was abandoned for DISK SAFETY, not for a weaker comparison. k is a column of every row and both sides partition identically, so per-partition multiset differences sum to the monolithic one exactly.

ATTRIBUTION_CORRECTION.what_I_filed_under_pd12: the segment-length census as pd12's incremental cost
ATTRIBUTION_CORRECTION.correct: pd12 needs NO open-segment replay at all. Its incrementality is: append newly available rows once the required EMA states already exist. The 772,433 open-segment bars (7.27%) are an A2-STACK figure carried by the upstream EMA producer, NOT a pd12 recomputation requirement.

SEGMENT_CENSUS_A2_STACK.tail: 0.42% of segments hold 39.2% of all COMPLETE bars
SEGMENT_CENSUS_A2_STACK.belongs_to: the upstream stateful producers (EMA, and later stageC4 / STAGE_D_R2), not pd12

READABLE_PARTIAL_OUTPUT_fixture.mechanism_added: A2_PARTITION_COMPLETION_V1 — a partition is COMPLETE only on run_id + partition identity + family + byte size + output digest + row reconciliation + an explicit COMPLETED marker. 'file exists and parquet is readable' is NOT completion.
READABLE_PARTIAL_OUTPUT_fixture.atomicity: data written to .tmp, fsync, atomic rename; the old marker is removed BEFORE the rewrite so a crash can never leave a marker outliving its data
cases: crash artefact is genuinely READABLE and correctly typed
readable partial is NOT accepted as COMPLETE
rejection reason is digest/size reconciliation, not readability
no marker -> NOT COMPLETE (file exists and is readable)
marker claiming COMPLETED cannot rescue wrong data
recovered digest equals the honest write
refused write leaves the prior bytes intact and internally COMPLETE
but it is NOT CURRENT for this run (stale-run guard)
after this run writes it, it IS current

FIXTURE_EXPECTATION_CORRECTED.disclosure: one fixture assertion was CHANGED AFTER IT FAILED. Disclosed deliberately because this is the exact shape of fitting a test to its result.
FIXTURE_EXPECTATION_CORRECTED.original_assertion: 'a refused write leaves the partition INCOMPLETE, not silently current'
FIXTURE_EXPECTATION_CORRECTED.why_it_was_wrong: a rejected short write must NOT destroy validated prior data. Leaving the good bytes intact is correct behaviour, and the original expectation would have made the safe behaviour a failure.
FIXTURE_EXPECTATION_CORRECTED.what_was_NOT_done: the assertion was not merely relaxed or deleted
FIXTURE_EXPECTATION_CORRECTED.what_WAS_done: the real hazard behind it — a stale-but-internally-complete partition being adopted as THIS run's output, the STALE RESULT FILE READ AS CURRENT class — was addressed by ADDING a run_id currency guard to is_complete(). The fixture now asserts BOTH halves: the bytes stay internally COMPLETE, AND they are NOT CURRENT for a different run_id.
FIXTURE_EXPECTATION_CORRECTED.net: the suite grew from 13 to 15 assertions and is strictly stronger than before

INPUT_ORDER.canonical_behaviour: the wrapper sorts by bar_start on load (ORDER BY) and reindexes EMA to the bar index; incidental order is never relied upon
